text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT SALE - Philippine flour millers bought 18,900 tonnes of U.S. western white wheat at $188 to $189 per tonne through trading firm Mitsui and Co Ltd, traders said. Philippine millers also asked for quotations for another 21,100 tonnes of U.S. dark northern spring wheat with 13.5 percent and 14 percent protein content.
- Tunisia bought 175,000 tonnes of optional origin soft wheat at $179.87 and $176.87 per tonne for October, November and December shipment.
WHEAT SALE cont'd - South Korea's Dae Han Flour Mills Co Ltd bought 23,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat from Japan's Mitsui and Company. Shipment was set for January 5-February 5 to Inchon.

- Two South Korean flour mills, Dongah Flour Mills Co Ltd and Cheiljedang Corp, on Thursday bought a total of 22,500 tonnes of U.S. No. 1 wheat from Japanese trading house Mitsubishi Corp, traders said. Shipment was set for December 10-January 10 from the Pacific Northwest to the southeastern port cities of Pusan and Ulsan.

WHEAT AND BARLEY SALE - Japan's Food Agency bought 80,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat, 50,000 of Canadian wheat and 20,000 of Canadian barley at its weekly tender for November shipment. It also bought 17,000 tonnes of Australian wheat for October shipment.

CORN AND SOYBEAN SALE - Taiwan Sugar Corp bought 20,000 tonnes of No.2 or better U.S. yellow corn and 10,000 tonnes of No.2 or better U.S. yellow soybeans from Cargill at a tender on Thursday, traders said. The maximum moisture limits for the shipment were specified at 14.5 percent for the corn and 13.5 percent for the soybeans.

SOYBEAN TENDER - South Korea said it will tender Sept 5 for 20,000 tonnes of U.S. No. 1 soybean. Bids will be opened Sept 6. Shipment was set for Sept 26-Oct 15 if from the U.S. Gulf or for October 11-30 if from the Pacific Northwest.

CORN TENDER - Jordan is seeking to buy 50,000 tonnes of U.S. Number 3 yellow corn in one lot for shipment in the first half of November, traders said. Offers of corn of better grade, or equivalent origin, would also be acceptable. Offers must be received by September 25. Jordan's annual consumption of yellow corn is around 400,000 to 500,000 tonnes.
CORN TENDER - Taiwan's Members Feed Industry Group will tender on Friday for a 56,000-tonne shipment of U.S. No.2 corn for October delivery, traders said.
WHEAT TENDER - The CCC said it will tender on September 12 for 8,000 tonnes of U.S. soft red winter wheat for donation to Jamaica. Offers are due on September 12.
- The CCC on Sept 10 seeks 19,860 tonnes of soft white wheat of which 15,340 is for donation to Ethiopia and 4,520 for Pakistan. Shipment is for Sept 25-Oct 20.
WHEAT TENDER cont'd - The CCC seeks a total of 23,500 tonnes of U.S. wheat under the export donation program to Honduras.

The deal includes 5,000 tonnes northern spring/dark northern spring wheat and 3,000 tonnes soft red winter wheat set for November 1-25 shipment. It also includes 9,500 NS/DNS wheat and 6,000 tonnes SRW wheat slated for December 10-30 shipment. Offers are due on September 11.
MARKET TALK - The U.S. is stepping up its barley export campaign to Japan, offering increasingly competitive prices compared to Canadian prices, Japanese officials said.

... The EU is unlikely to restore export subsidies for its wheat as long as some exporters are ready to pay an export tax, officials close the EU executive said on Thursday ... The EU will raise durum wheat import duties on Friday. Duties on transatlantic imports will be raised to 5.29 Ecus a tonne from zero while duties on nearby imports will rise to 15.29 Ecus from 8.55 Ecus.

A European Union sale of 183,411 tonnes of German intervention barley is worth $142 per tonne, FOB Germany, and is mostly destined for Saudi Arabia, European grain sources said on Thursday. The EU's cereals management committee sold 183,411 tonnes of German intervention barley at a minimum price of 103.69 Ecus per tonne.
Saudi Arabia provisionally bought 800,000 tonnes of optional-origin barley at an August 21 tender at prices between $160 and $162 CIF, traders said last week.
But European grain traders and officials said the Saudis may reduce the purchase to 600,000 tonnes.
